catalog_quote: Sochiapam Chinantec has seven tones and two types of syllable stress, so there is the possibility of 14 tone-stress contrasts on any monosyllabic word. The consonant-vowel combination of ta, for example, has the following meanings. ¹ is used to mark high tone, ² = mid tone, ³ = low tone, double numbers such as ¹³ indicate a tone glide from one level to the other. Ballistic syllable stress (intense and short) is indicated by accent on the nuclear vowel, controlled syllable stress (low-intensity and long) is unmarked. ta¹ will we arrive? tá¹ complete (adjective) ta² we arrive (habitually) tá² recently ta³ foot tá³ weaving (noun) ta¹³ let's fight tá¹³ I will chop ... Whistle speech, based on 31 etic tone-stress distinctions, is used by men to communicate complex messages with minimal ambiguity. ... Verbs are marked by change in tone, stress, or vowels, or a combination of these for person …

new_statements.quote: Speakers of the language can use more than thirty tone-stress distinctions to communicate messages in whistle speech with minimal ambiguity. The majority of words consist of a single syllable; there are a small number of two-syllable words and less than a dozen known tri-syllabics. This model-neutral presentation describes everything from the phonemes up through phrases and clauses to compound sentences; from the changes of tone and stress to changes in nucleus to signal a wide variety of tense, aspect, and related features.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Publisher-level statement only: a tone language in which tone combines with a 'stress' feature (the Chinantecan ballistic/controlled syllable-type contrast) into more than thirty tone-stress distinctions; tone-stress changes carry verbal inflection (tense, aspect, person). Most words are monosyllabic, so no positional word-stress rule is at issue; none is stated in the snippet.
new_statements.identity_note: All three listed works describe the same variety, the Chinantec of San Pedro Sochiapam (Foris's 'Sochiapan'), ISO cso = Glottolog soch1239; no other dialect is involved. Index 2 is a duplicate listing of index 0; the 1993 Auckland PhD thesis is the earlier version of the same grammar (SIL 'Has Version' cross-reference).

tone_statements.quote: Syllables are either ballistic, symbolized by an accent over the nuclear vowel, or controlled, with no accent. Together with these dynamic patterns there are three simple tones, high 1, mid 2) and low 3, and four sequences, two upglides 21 32, and two downglides 13 23, There is phonemic nasalization of the syllable nucleus, for example tan32 bird versus ta3¢ ladder.
